answer.evidence: In radon/visitors.py, ComplexityVisitor.__init__ stores no_assert (line 165). visit_Assert (around lines 257-260) does `self.complexity += not self.no_assert`, so an assertion adds 1 only when no_assert is False, i.e. when assertion counting is enabled. The flag is propagated to nested visitors at lines 279 and 313, so nested functions and class methods behave the same way. Review time goes mostly to the neighbouring modules. radon/raw.py needs a check that its line-counting logic is independent of this flag. radon/metrics.py needs a check of how it aggregates complexity and whether it passes or assumes a no_assert setting. A short pass over radon/complexity.py should confirm that the no_assert argument is passed to the visitor consistently.
